title: eventstream: chunk-order stabilizer, UTF-8-aware fragmenter, and function-call sentinel preservation
author: Evelyn Chen
description:
Context and motivation:

Production telemetry and customer reports showed a class of failures where the OpenAI-compatible eventstream adapter would emit partial JSON objects or lose function-call sentinel boundaries when upstream transport delivered fragments out-of-order or when multi-byte UTF-8 sequences were split across network frames. These manifest as: truncated JSON in streaming clients, tool/function-calling errors from the compatibility layer, and occasional token-level scrambling when small concurrent reassembly windows overlap.

This PR introduces a conservative, low-latency reassembly strategy (v2) that: 1) attaches a lightweight chunk sequence tag to every inbound fragment at the transport boundary, 2) performs UTF-8-aware fragment concatenation to avoid breaking multi-byte codepoints, 3) implements a configurable reordering window with a fast-path for single-fragment messages to avoid added latency, and 4) guarantees that function-call sentinels (tool markers) are only emitted once the coalescer has validated boundary completeness.

What changed (high-level):
- New coalescer: serving/eventstream/coalescer.go — deterministic ordering by sequence+receive-ts with a configurable reorder window (default 30ms).
- UTF-8-safe fragmenter: serving/eventstream/fragmenter.go — detects and preserves incomplete codepoints when splitting/combining frames.
- OpenAI compatibility adapter: api/openai/stream_adapter.go — waits for sentinel-complete frames before emitting structured function-call events and adds a small safety-check to avoid duplicate sentinel emission.
- Feature flag and defaults: pkg/feature_flags/flags.go, pkg/config/defaults.go — feature.sse_reassembly_v2 gate and streaming.reassembly_window_ms default.
- Metrics and tracing: console/metrics_registry.go — new metrics: eventstream.reassembly.lat_ms, eventstream.reassembly.missed_windows, eventstream.reassembly.fastpath_hits.
- Tests: tests/integration/eventstream_reassembly_test.py and tests/unit/fragmenter_test.go — deterministic reorder/corruption simulation harnesses and UTF-8 split cases.
- Docs: docs/streaming.md — new section describing the reassembly window and tuning guidance for low-latency workloads.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Reorder window default is 30ms: chosen from bench results to fix real-world interleaving cases while keeping median extra latency < 3ms for typical packet distributions.
- Fast-path for single-fragment messages: avoids touching the reassembler for most small responses (reduces P50 latency impact to negligible).
- Explicit sequence tags are lightweight and scoped to the process boundary (we do not change external wire protocol — tags are attached/removed at transport boundary).

Backwards compatibility:
- The feature is behind feature.sse_reassembly_v2 and enabled by default; in environments that cannot tolerate any change, ops can turn it off. The OpenAI compatibility guarantees (function-call sentinel semantics) are preserved; this PR prevents accidental duplicate sentinel emission.

- [x] Added metrics and tracing hooks

- fix(fragmenter): UTF-8-aware fragment concat and preserve incomplete codepoints
- feat(adapter): hold emission until sentinel-complete; add duplicate-sentinel guard
- perf: add fast-path bypass for single-fragment messages and benchmark harness
- test: integration harness for reorder and corruption cases
- ci: add reassembly tests to streaming job and flake guard

Illustrative snippet (coalescer ordering):
```go
// ordering key: (seq, receiveTs)
if a.seq != b.seq {
  return a.seq < b.seq
}
return a.receiveTs.Before(b.receiveTs)
```

CI and review history: single-run CI initially failed on lint + go vet (forgot to run gofmt in coalescer). After fix and force-push CI passed (unit+integration streaming job).

Review conversation (high-level):
- Marco Ruiz (review): "Please justify the 30ms default. Also add a stress test for high-concurrency degraded networks — we saw flakiness in previous iterations."
- Author (Evelyn): "Added microbench results in PR comment and new stress harness. Fast-path keeps added median latency small; stress test included and stable on my runs."
- Nadia Ibrahim (review): "Can the sequence tag be replayed across a reconnect? Concern about duplicate seqs if transport reconnects."
- Author: "Sequence tags are ephemeral and scoped to the connection; adapter drops tags on reconnect. Documented in streaming.md. If a client reconnects, we treat as new stream — no duplication semantics exposed externally."
- Carlos Mendes (approve): "Verified against OpenAI compatibility tool: preserved function-call semantics in all test cases."

Merge outcome: merged via squash with merge commit a1b2c3d4e5f67890; release notes below.

release_notes: Fixed streaming reassembly to prevent partial-JSON and sentinel-loss when fragments arrive out-of-order. Added UTF-8-aware fragment handling and a configurable reordering window (default 30ms) to balance correctness and latency. Metrics added for reassembly latency and fast-path hits. Feature gated under feature.sse_reassembly_v2; ops can toggle if needed.
notes_for_ops: Tuning: set streaming.reassembly_window_ms to 0 to disable reordering (fastest path) or lower to 10ms for ultra-low-latency clusters. Enable tracing flag eventstream.reassembly.debug to collect sample traces for debugging.\n
impact_summary: This change reduces incidents of malformed JSON and lost function-call boundaries in streamed responses. Benchmarked median P50 latency bump <3ms with fast-path enabled; P99 unchanged in typical traffic. Ops should monitor eventstream.reassembly.missed_windows to tune the window.
